entities.summary: Saad al-Dawla ibn جafস ibn ااfস ibn Muhassib al-Dawla al-Abhar঒ was a Jewish physician and statesman in thirteenth-century Persia (Iran). He was born into a prominent family and received a traditional Jewish education in Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek. Al-Dawla's medical expertise was highly regarded, and he wrote several influential medical texts. He served as a physician to the Mongol king, Hulagu Khan, and played a key role in the administration of the Mongol Empire's territories in Persia. Al-Dawla's legacy can be seen in the continued practice of Jewish medicine in Iran and the transmission of his medical knowledge to future generations. His contributions to the field of medicine were recognized by the Islamic Golden Age, and he is considered one of the most important Jewish physicians of the Middle Ages. Al-Dawla's significance extends beyond his medical achievements, as he represents the intersection of Jewish, Mongol, and Islamic cultures in the medieval world.
